data.title: Fitch Lowers France's Outlook to Negative From Stable
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Fitch Ratings said it was lowering its outlook on France's credit rating to negative from Stable, while affirming the country's A+ ratings.

The move comes as France faces economic and social pressure over its debt and growing borrowing costs. In recent weeks, hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Paris and other French cities, with some protesters resorting to vandalism and violence.

Fitch said the negative outlook reflects a deterioration since its August review, and cited weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit. These factors are worsening debt dynamics from an already weak starting point, Fitch added.

Yields on France's government bonds have also risen since the last review, Fitch said. The agency said it now forecasts interest payments will increase to 3.3% of GDP in 2028 from 2.5% of GDP in 2025. Fitch also sees France's deficit at 5.5% of GDP in 2027, which it said reflects a weaker growth assessment and the risk of concessions during the budget process.

The country's A+ rating is supported by a large, wealthy and diversified economy, strong institutions, euro area membership and a resilient banking sector, Fitch added.

The next scheduled review date for France's rating hasn't yet been set, Fitch said, but added it expects to review the rating by end-February 2027 at the latest.

data.title: Binance Hit By Record $6.3 Bln Crypto Hack
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, suffered a $6.3 billion security breach in what analysts described as potentially the largest financial theft ever recorded.

The exchange halted withdrawals after hackers compromised its transaction approval system and transferred assets from an internet-connected wallet. Binance said customer funds remain safe and it has set aside about $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the losses. Around $3 billion of the affected assets have so far been located or frozen.

Blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis said the attack showed similarities to previous cryptocurrency thefts attributed to North Korea. Binance is working with U.S. authorities, including the FBI and Secret Service, as investigators trace the stolen funds.

Tether froze nearly $1.57 billion linked to the breach, while Circle froze more than $800 million. The attack also pressured cryptocurrency markets, with bitcoin falling to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether dropping more than 3 percent to a two-month low of $2,178.

data.title: Adicet Bio Reports Inducement Grant under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
data.description:
Adicet Bio, Inc. (), a clinical stage biotechnology company discovering and developing allogeneic gamma delta CAR-T cell and in vivo CAR T therapies for autoimmune diseases, hematologic malignancies and solid tumors, today announced it granted an inducement award on October 30, 2026.

One individual was hired by Adicet in October 2026 and granted new hire non-qualified stock options to purchase 1,500 shares of Adicet’s common stock with an exercise price of $3.42 per share, the closing price of Adicet’s common stock as reported by Nasdaq on October 30, 2026. One-fourth of the shares underlying the employee’s option will vest on the one-year anniversary of the employee’s start date and thereafter the remaining three-fourths of the shares underlying the employee’s option will vest in thirty-six substantially equal monthly installments, such that the shares underlying the option granted to the employee will be fully vested on the fourth anniversary of the employee’s start date, subject to the employee’s continued employment with Adicet on such vesting dates.

The above-described award was granted outside of Adicet’s stockholder-approved equity incentive plans pursuant to Adicet’s 2022 Inducement Plan (the Inducement Plan), which was adopted by the board of directors in January 2022 and subsequently amended in January 2023. The award was authorized by the compensation committee of the board of directors, which is comprised solely of independent directors, as a material inducement to the employee entering into employment with Adicet in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

About Adicet Bio, Inc.

Adicet Bio, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company discovering and developing a broad pipeline of allogeneic gamma delta T cell therapies, engineered with chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), alongside differentiated in vivo CAR-T therapies with the potential to redefine treatment across autoimmune diseases, hematologic malignancies and solid tumors. For more information, please visit our website at https://www.adicetbio.com.

data.title: 13D Filings — Barrons.com
data.description:
These disclosures are from 13Ds filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 13Ds are filed within 10 days of an entity's attaining more than 5% in any class of a company's securities. Subsequent changes in holdings or intentions must be reported in amended filings. This material is from Oct. 22 through Oct. 28, 2026. Source: VerityData

Activist Filings

Mattel (MAT) EdgePoint Investment Group filed an initial 13D regarding its stake in the toy and games maker, shifting to the stance of an activist investor from previous disclosures in a passive 13G. EdgePoint reported that it sold 106,627 Mattel shares from Aug. 24 through Sept. 28 at per share prices ranging from $13.25 to $14.48.

After the departure of former Chairman and CEO Ynon Kreiz, Mattel invited EdgePoint to propose a board nominee, and on Oct. 21 it appointed EdgePoint partner Lee Matheson to Mattel's board under a cooperation agreement. Following the latest sales, EdgePoint continues to own 50,515,811 Mattel shares, or 17.7% of those outstanding. Shares of Mattel have lost about 24% of their value in 2026.

Original Filings

Empire State Realty Trust (ESRT) Erez Asset Management disclosed a new position in the office and retail REIT of 10,000,000 shares. Erez Asset Management purchased those shares from Sept. 2 through Oct. 2 at per share prices ranging from $4.08 to $4.46. Following the latest purchases, Erez owns an initial 5.8% stake in Empire State Realty's outstanding stock. Shares of Empire State Realty have lost about 23.9% of their value in 2026.

Increases in Holdings

Dole (DOLE) Pale Fire Capital raised its stake in the fresh-produce company to 9,634,264 shares. Pale Fire did so through the purchase of 206,788 Dole shares from Oct. 9 through Oct. 12 at per share prices ranging from $13.05 to $13.28. Following the latest purchases, Pale Fire owns a 10.2% stake in Dole's outstanding stock. Shares of Dole have lost roughly 10.1% of their value in 2026.

Decreases in Holdings

Koppers Holdings (KOP) Simcoe Capital Management lowered its stake in the treated wood products and chemicals company to 1,063,279 shares. Simcoe did so through the sale of 331,977 Koppers Holdings shares from Oct. 1 through Oct. 22 at per share prices ranging from $41.02 to $47.17. Following the latest sales, Simcoe continues to own a 5.6% stake in Koppers' outstanding stock. Shares of Koppers have gained about 56.9% in value in 2026.

Elastic (ESTC) Pictet Asset Management lowered its stake in the data analytics software company to 5,217,779 shares. Pictet did so through the sale of 286,843 Elastic shares from Oct. 6 through Oct. 26 at per share prices ranging from $91.74 to $106.06, and partially offset those sales through the purchase of 59,500 shares from Oct. 6 through Oct. 20 at $91.30 to $98.23.

Following the latest activity, Pictet continues to own a 4.9% stake in Elastic's outstanding stock, placing Pictet below the 5% threshold that would require it to report further sales. Shares of Elastic have gained roughly 45.8% in value since the beginning of this year.

data.title: Fitch revises France's outlook to 'negative' on worsening debt dynamics
data.description:
Credit ratings agency Fitch on Friday revised France's outlook to "negative" from "stable", warning that deteriorating fiscal conditions and political fragmentation are undermining debt stabilization prospects.

The agency pointed to weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit since its August review, compounded by a fractured political landscape that is making sustained fiscal consolidation harder to deliver.

The move heightens the risk of a future downgrade for the euro zone's second-largest economy, which has already seen its borrowing costs climb sharply, weighing on its debt outlook.

"The emerging policy debate ahead of the presidential election has not materially strengthened Fitch's confidence in the prospects for durable deficit reduction that could lead to debt stabilization," the agency said.

data.title: SpaceX's Shotwell says 2 million shares to be gifted to children's Trump Accounts
data.description:
SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said in an X post on Friday that more than 2 million of the company's shares will be distributed to eligible children through "Trump Accounts" in December.

Here are some more details:

  • The initial gift of shares, currently being transferred to escrow, will go to children aged 11 to 17 living in ZIP codes with a median family income of $57,000 or less, Shotwell said

  • Children living in ZIP codes with too few residents for median family income data to be reported will also be eligible

  • Eligible families should receive a notice by Monday, she said

  • A separate gift is expected to be finalized in coming weeks for eligible children in military families serving overseas, children in foster care, and children whose family income is $90,000 or less, living in eligible Texas counties

  • CEO Elon Musk said earlier this month that SpaceX and Tesla had formed special committees to explore a potential merger, though he said the panels had not agreed upon transaction terms and might never do so

data.title: Inovio surges 300% following FDA approval of Voceryq for rare disease
data.description:
Key points:
  • Inovio Pharmaceuticals is up ~300% in after-hours trading Friday after the US FDA announced it has approved Voceryq (doruxapapogene ralaplasmid and lalikinogene sifuplasmid-gxfd) as a treatment for the rare disease recurrent respiratory papillomatosis (RRP).
  • The approval is the first for a plasmid DNA-based immunotherapy in the US.
  • RRP is characterized by small, wart-like growths in the airways. The condition is caused by human papillomavirus.
  • Accelerated approval was granted based on data indicating that Voceryq helped reduce the frequency of surgical procedures needed to remove growths in adults, meeting an intermediate clinical endpoint.
  • Inovio will need to conduct a post-marketing study to confirm the therapy's benefit.
  • The FDA said that the treatment is "designed to stimulate the immune system to respond to and attack cells infected by the specific types of HPV that cause RRP (types 6 and 11)."

data.title: Midterm US elections, earnings, jobs data loom for AI-wary stock market
data.description:
Key points:
  • Investors eye possible Democratic win in Congress, potential AI impact from vote
  • Apple, AMD, Palantir among Q3 reports due in coming week
  • Monthly jobs report on Friday comes after Fed holds rates steady

By Lewis Krauskopf

US midterm elections, a heavy slate of corporate earnings and the monthly jobs report will further test stock investors next week, after a series of setbacks for the market-leading AI trade.

The latest AI turbulence stemmed from disappointing quarterly results of Alphabet and Amazon , two hyperscalers spending massively on data centers, while shares of semiconductor company Intel tumbled nearly 29% on Friday following its report.

Dragged down by tech and AI-related stocks, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX sank 1.8% on Friday while the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.9%.

The quarterly results intensified concerns about financing and financial returns needed to support the AI investment theme at the heart of the US bull stock market. The questions are likely to persist, with Apple , AMD and Palantir among the major tech and AI players due to report next week. Also, the midterm elections could determine the outlook for AI regulation.

The stock market "seems a bit troubled to me, and I think that really stems from the AI fears that seem to be persistent, if not building," said Marta Norton, chief investment strategist at retirement and wealth services provider Empower. "There is still some digestion around what we saw with earnings this week."

MIDTERM VOTE COULD AFFECT AI

Tuesday's elections will determine whether Democrats can wrest control of Congress away from President Donald Trump's Republican party. Democrats are widely predicted to win the House of Representatives, but the Senate is more in doubt. Republicans controlled both chambers of Congress during the first two years of the Trump administration.

Investors are bracing for increasing pushback on data centers, whose impact on energy costs and the environment has led to intense public opposition. Despite doubts that any viable legislation will pose serious risks to AI investment, regardless of which party wins, a Democratic sweep is expected to bring more scrutiny. Investors are also watching local and state races in Texas and elsewhere on Tuesday for their implications for the data-center buildout.

"To the extent that the Democrats really do have a significant blue wave, I think that will be seen as negative for both the AI names, for tech to some extent in general, and maybe even for the market as a whole," said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments.

Defense and healthcare are other stock market areas that could be sensitive to the election results. Any shift in Washington could affect the outlook for fiscal spending that could reverberate through asset prices. A Democratic sweep could bring more regulatory scrutiny, including for Wall Street banks and crypto firms.

ALSO ON TAP: APPLE, AMD RESULTS, JOBS DATA

Robust earnings performance has underpinned equity gains so far in 2026. With over half of the S&P 500 having reported third-quarter results, overall earnings were on pace to rise 31.6% for the period, according to LSEG IBES data on Friday.

Investors were punishing some reports. For example, Caterpillar shares sank 9% on Thursday after the company stuck to its annual sales growth forecast despite strong demand for its power equipment from data centers.

"The earnings bar is very high," said Chris Galipeau, head market strategist at the Franklin Templeton Institute. "And if you miss or don't jump over that bar, you're in trouble."

Apple reports on Monday, with the iPhone maker's shares up about 27% so far this year. Results are also expected from semiconductor companies AMD and Qualcomm as well as Palantir, which offers another view of the AI trade. McDonald's , Amgen and ConocoPhillips are among over 100 S&P 500 companies that are due to report next week.

Next Friday's employment report for October will give a critical read into the health of the US economy.

Data on Thursday showed the US economy in the third quarter grew at its fastest pace in a year, as consumers maintained robust spending and businesses doubled down on investment in AI. The Federal Reserve this week upgraded its assessment of the economy as it held interest rates steady.

"I think the missing piece of this strong economic growth narrative is the lack of job growth," said Matthew Miskin, co-chief investment strategist at Manulife John Hancock Investments.

Other areas of the market have picked up the slack as AI and related technology stocks have struggled. For October, the energy and financial sectors posted solid monthly gains, as did defensive groups such as utilities and healthcare. The S&P 500 was last up over 10% on the year.

"The market is much more broad than people generally want to give it credit for," Galipeau said.
